From: Alex Pierce <ops@fastflow.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: bulk promo credit issuance for new cohort

Hi Tessa,

We rolled a small user acquisition campaign yesterday and are seeing a surge of signups. Marketing asked if Redwood can top up promo credits for the cohort so we can run in-product experiments this week. I attached the signup export (emails + user ids).

Quick context: about ~430 accounts created in a 2-hour window, many from @fastflow.ai subdomains and some personal-looking emails. Can your team do a bulk issuance of the $50 promo to these accounts? If you need a smaller cohort we can supply a curated list.

Thanks — appreciate any fast path.

Alex Pierce
Director, Operations | FastFlow AI
ops@fastflow.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: bulk promo credit issuance for new cohort

Tessa / Neha,

FYI — I pulled the FastFlow list Alex attached and ran it through the signup-fraud pipeline (v3 rules). High-level findings:
- 418 unique accounts in 118 minutes (very high velocity).
- ~72% created from disposable/dynamic domains (temp-mail, mailinator variants).
- Common sign-up fingerprint: same user-agent string and identical client_time offsets across many events.
- 38 accounts share the same /24 IPv4 blocks (likely bot farm or corporate NAT).

I've attached a short CSV with suspicious flags (suspicious_signups_20260520.csv) and a one-pager IP summary (ip_summary_20260520.txt). My recommendation: hold bulk issuance and require manual verification for any account we credit. If this is a legitimate FastFlow-backed campaign, we'd prefer they provide an allowlist (CSR or SSO list) rather than issuing broadly.

Thanks Dev — good catch. Alex, looping our fraud team since there are suspicious signals in the list.

A couple quick asks before we take action:
1) Dev / Neha — can you cross-check the IPs and vendor UA against our known bot signatures and confirm if these are outright botnets or possibly corporate NAT from FastFlow offices?
2) Alex — can you confirm whether this campaign used a marketing partner or an external acquisition vendor? If so, can you share the vendor domain and any expected allowlists (SSO domains, CIDR ranges)?

Short-term I'm going to place a manual hold on mass promo issuance while we triage. If the list has valid FastFlow employees, we can do a targeted, verified issuance (SSO or email verification). If it's a mix with lots of throws, we'll deny the bulk top-up and offer a safe alternative (one-off verified credits + promo link).

I know this delays the experiment — let's try to keep it to under 24 hours.

Quick update — I ran an IP backfill and looked up MX records for the email hosts. Findings:
- ~310 accounts from disposable hostnames (MX resolves to known temp-mail providers).
- ~56 accounts appear to be legitimate corporate emails under fastflow.ai or subdomains we can validate.
- The /24 clusters Dev flagged are spread across three cloud provider ASN ranges that match bot farm patterns in our threat intel.

Suggested disposition:
- Deny bulk automatic issuance.
- Allow immediate $50 credit to the 56 validated fastflow.ai addresses once Alex confirms a canonical allowlist.
- Offer FastFlow: a one-time extension promo for up to 10 verified pilot users and recommend SSO provisioning for future campaigns.

I'll attach the small allowlist CSV (validated_allowlist_56.csv). If Alex confirms, we can push credits by EOD after a manual check.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Trust & Safety Analyst
Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the patience. Summary and next steps below.

Summary of our review:
- We identified a high-confidence bot pattern across the bulk signup list (disposable domains, UA fingerprinting, /24 IP clustering).
- Approximately 56 addresses are validated as fastflow.ai corporate or subdomain accounts.

Outcome:
- We cannot authorize a blanket bulk issuance for the entire cohort as submitted.
- We will provision $50 promo credits to the 56 validated addresses once FastFlow confirms the canonical allowlist (attach validated_allowlist_56.csv). Please reply with confirmation and the preferred deadline for issuance.
- As a goodwill gesture we will offer FastFlow a one-time extension coupon for 10 additional verified pilot users (manual verification required). This coupon is single-use and subject to our anti-abuse checks.

Recommendations for future campaigns:
- Use SSO/SCIM provisioning or a verified allowlist (CIDR or domain list) for large pilot cohorts. This avoids manual holds and prevents bot exploitation.
- If you work with an acquisition partner, ask them for a signed attestation or partner ID; we can whitelist partner-sourced cohorts after a short vetting step.

If you want to escalate to an account exec or legal for contract-level guarantees, loop in your Redwood contact.

Best,
